rektion: jdm./einer Sache (Dat.) zuhören (gespannt, aufmerksam, geduldig zuhören)
definition_de: aufmerksam hören, was jemand sagt oder erzählt (Hör mir doch mal zu!); anders als 'hören', das auch ohne Absicht passiert.
example_de: Die Enkel hörten ganz gespannt zu, als die Oma von ihrer Kindheit auf dem Bauernhof erzählte.
example_en: The grandchildren listened with rapt attention as grandma talked about her childhood on the farm.
visual_idea: Collocation 'gespannt zuhören': a grandmother in an armchair tells a story with lively gestures, and three grandchildren on the rug lean forward with chins on their hands and wide eyes. The forward-leaning bodies show active listening, the difference to plain 'hören'. No book (that would be 'vorlesen', and books attract text). Rejected: a lecture hall (students on phones read as 'nicht zuhören') and comforting a friend (reads as 'trösten').
image_prompt: a cosy living room in the evening, an elderly grandmother sits in an old armchair and tells a story with lively hand gestures and a warm smile, three grandchildren sit on the rug in front of her and lean forward with their chins on their hands, eyes wide and mouths slightly open, completely absorbed, a crackling fireplace beside them, warm firelight, medium wide shot
negative_prompt: text, letters, watermark, signature, caption, blurry, extra fingers, deformed hands, cluttered background, multiple panels
video_prompt: a grandmother in an armchair tells a story with lively gestures; the three grandchildren on the rug lean further forward, then laugh together at a funny moment and lean in again; static medium wide shot, warm firelight
